description: I'm passionate about space, science, and game development. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I want to create MARS: LAST SIGNAL, a Mars survival game using real NASA data. I'm looking for teammates skilled in coding, 3D design, UI/UX, research, or storytelling. Beginners are welcome! Let's build something amazing together!
summary:
On Mars there is no GPS, no roads, and Earth is 3 to 22 minutes away by signal. Future explorers must make life-or-death decisions alone, and a normal map only draws a line; it cannot say whether that line is safe.

Orbitalnyx Marswalk HUD is a navigation and decision companion for people training to explore Mars, built around Jezero Crater. The user picks where they are and where they want to go. Orbitalnyx layers NASA Mars data, blocks slopes steeper than 15 degrees, plans a route through three science stops, and always plans the way home. It compares routes on steepness, rocky ground, distance, dust and energy, then shows one clear status: GO, CAUTION or TURN BACK.

It addresses Challenge #10 (Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map) with multi-layer NASA data, automatic hazard flagging, science-target route planning, an astronaut-focused interface (Tablet and Helmet HUD modes) and links to rover point-of-view imagery.

Safety decisions come from fixed, checkable rules in code. AI only explains results in two or three plain lines and never overrides an alert.

Built for space-training crews, analog-mission teams, astronaut candidates and private space travellers, Orbitalnyx is a training and planning prototype today, with simulated telemetry. Next steps: real HiRISE slope data, boulder detection, offline mode and validation against rover traverse logs.

Live app: https://orbitalnyx.netlify.app
details:
WHAT IT IS

Orbitalnyx is a prototype GPS-style navigation system for Mars, designed to be very easy to use. There is no real GPS on Mars, so the user selects their current location on a map of Jezero Crater, picks a destination, and Orbitalnyx works out the easiest and most efficient route between the two.

WHAT IT DOES

- Lets the user choose their location and destination in a few simple steps.

- Compares possible routes on everything that matters for a walk on Mars: steepness, rocky ground, distance, dust and energy use.

- Blocks slopes steeper than 15 degrees and always plans the way back home.

- Gives one clear status, GO, CAUTION or TURN BACK, so the user does not have to read pages of data when time matters.

- Recommends the safest, fastest or lowest-effort route, and explains why in two or three plain sentences.

HOW IT WORKS

The app layers NASA Mars map and terrain data (Mars Trek) over Jezero Crater. Fixed rules in code calculate slope, distance, route cost and the GO / CAUTION / TURN BACK status, so every decision can be checked. AI is used only to explain results in simple words and never overrides a safety alert. Oxygen, battery and suit-pressure values are simulated for training, and slope, dust and radiation values are illustrative unless stated otherwise.

BENEFITS

Normal maps only draw a line. Orbitalnyx compares many factors at once and tells the user whether the route is safe, so one screen replaces searching through manuals. It is built for space-training crews, analog-mission teams, astronaut candidates and private space travellers.

GOALS

Today: a training and planning prototype. Next: real HiRISE terrain data for accurate slopes, boulder detection, an offline mode, and validation against Perseverance and Curiosity traverse logs.

TOOLS USED

NASA Mars Trek and Mars Fact Sheet data; GitHub Copilot (code); Pavo AI (demo video); Gamma (slides); ChatGPT and Claude (research and drafting); Instaplay (training game); Netlify (hosting). Live app: https://orbitalnyx.netlify.app
